description:
FOUND s473t5e (#1501 round 6, `re/` CHECK 2).  t/re/begin-once.t is DIFF 1/1:

    not ok 1 - /o done at begin is preserved and a new string does not match
    ok 2     - /o done at begin is preserved and the original string matches

perl's `/o` compiles an interpolated pattern ONCE, at first execution, and
never again -- so a later change to the interpolated variable does NOT change
what the pattern matches.  PCL memoises a regex by its SOURCE TEXT
(`*p-regex-op-cache*`), which is the opposite rule: when the interpolated text
changes, the pattern changes.

ROWS: 1, and this is the only file that tests it.  Its value is not the row --
it is that `/o` is a documented perl modifier PCL silently ignores, and a CPAN
module that relies on it (the idiom is `/$re/o` inside a loop) gets a
DIFFERENT MATCH, not merely a slower one.

SHAPE: `/o` is a property of the match SITE, so the memo key has to be the site
rather than the text -- which the emitter can give it (a per-site cell, the way
`state` is lowered) without the runtime guessing.  Decide first whether it is
worth it: the pragmatic alternative is a `docs/not-supported.md` entry saying
`/o` is ignored, which is honest and costs this one row.  Do NOT half-do it by
keying the existing text cache differently: that changes every non-/o pattern's
identity as well.
subject: the `/o` (compile-once) modifier is not honoured: a pattern compiled at BEGIN recompiles for a new interpolated string, so t/re/begin-once.t's one assertion fails
